Subject: GPU fleet recommendation for Crestline - initial ask

Ben / Nicole —

Thanks for sharing the workload breakdown earlier. I dug into the sample traces you sent (thank you) and pulled together a quick inventory of the dominant query patterns so we can map them to candidate GPU types. Attached is a CSV with the per-model peak memory, average seq length, and a rough tokens/sec estimate derived from the traces (crestline_workload_profiles.csv).

Top-level observations:
- Two high-memory, large-context models (seq lengths 8k-12k) used for extractive summarization and long-form Q&A.
- A medium-sized generation model used for guided content creation (~2k seq) that is latency-sensitive during interactive sessions.
- High-throughput embedding requests (short contexts, batchable) for semantic search and reranking.
- Occasional peaks where the platform needs to sustain bursts up to ~150 qps for embeddings during morning syncs.

Question for the team (Marissa / Karthik): given Crestline's requirement for a 95th percentile latency SLO of 200ms for the interactive generation path, and a hard memory-driven capacity need for the summarization models, what's your initial read on H100 vs A100 vs L4 suitability and a recommended split for Dedicated?

I want to align on a preliminary recommendation we can present on tomorrow's pricing call.

Thanks,
Diego
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Diego / Ben —

Nice breakdown — I pulled a short set of bench runs and put the high-level numbers into an XLSX (h100_a100_l4_perf_matrix.xlsx). Key takeaways from my runs against the representative models:
- Summarization models (long context): H100 gives best end-to-end throughput when using flash-attention kernels + bf16; memory headroom on A100 80GB is tight at peak batch sizes.
- Interactive generator (~2k seq): A100 40/80GB hits target latency in many cases and is cheaper per-hour than H100; using quantization-aware kernels reduces memory footprint but adds a small tail latency risk.
- Embeddings: L4 instances are materially cheaper and achieve equivalent embedding quality for the short-context models; throughput per dollar favors L4 when batched.

I've sketched three candidate fleet mixes (sheet: "mixes"):
A) Performance-first: 60% H100 / 30% A100 / 10% L4 — targets tight latency SLOs but higher cost
B) Balanced: 30% H100 / 50% A100 / 20% L4 — middle ground, keeps cost reasonable while preserving memory availability
C) Cost-first: 10% H100 / 60% A100 / 30% L4 — minimizes spend, relies on model quantization and caching to keep latency acceptable

I'll flag that the summarization models really push memory; if Ben wants a single-GPU packing strategy for those workloads the H100 80GB (HBM) is the safer bet. Happy to present these three mixes on the call.

--Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Marissa / team —

I pushed the mixes through a quick capacity model to translate Crestline's 95th-percentile traffic profile into instance counts. Below is a condensed excerpt (numbers rounded up):

Assumptions (from Diego's CSV + bench runs):
- Summarization model: 12k tokens context, peak concurrent sessions 8, per-session throughput requirement ~10 tok/sec (interactive extractive use is CPU-light but memory-heavy)
- Generator (interactive): target 95p latency = 200ms, typical sequence length ~2k, workload sustains 40 concurrent interactive sessions at peak
- Embeddings: burstable to 150 qps, average batch size 32 during steady-state 50 qps

Recommended Dedicated fleet (Balanced approach, 95% SLO-safe):
- H100 80GB: 6 GPUs (serve the 12k-context summarization models, plus headroom for canary/rollouts)
- A100 80GB: 10 GPUs (primary for interactive generator and mid-size models)
- L4 48GB equivalent: 8 GPUs (batch embeddings, rerank, low-latency cheap paths)

Rationale and operational notes:
- Memory headroom: The summarization models are single-GPU memory-bound. A100 80GB is possible but leaves less headroom for spikes; H100 provides both memory and better mixed-precision perf which reduces latency for long sequences.
- Cost trade: Per-hour cost (list) H100 > A100 > L4. The above mix attempts to limit H100 to only the memory-critical fleet so we don't overprovision expensive capacity.
- Autoscaling and fallback: Add an autoscale policy to burst embeddings onto A100 when L4 pool is saturated for short windows (with fallback routing). Also configure KV/prefix cache for the generator to reduce repeat-token compute.
- Canary/rollout: Reserve 1-2 GPUs in each pool for canary testing for model updates.

Operational impact on pricing: This mix maps closely to a reserved capacity proposal with a small burst credit band. If sales wants an aggressive cost plan, we can move to the Cost-first mix and rely on quantized model variants + denser packing; that will need tightened SLOs and more aggressive caching.

I'll attach a short PDF with the capacity math and a recommended canary schedule (crestline_capacity_proposal.pdf). If Ben is comfortable, I can convert these counts into a monthly reserved capacity quote for the pricing call.

-Karthik
Head of Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
